built-in.name: system
built-in.description: A software system, as shown on a C4 system context diagram.

built-in.name: container
built-in.description: A separately runnable or deployable unit, or a data store, within a system.

built-in.name: component
built-in.description: A grouping of related code within a container.

built-in.name: library
built-in.description: A library artifact that other code depends on but that is not deployed on its own. It has no C4 level: a library is not a container, and a thin service and its library are drawn as one container.

built-in.name: module
built-in.description: A build module, such as a Maven module. It has no C4 level: a module is a unit of the build, not a container or component.

built-in.name: package
built-in.description: A Java package. It has no C4 level: a package is a way to group code, not a component.

built-in.name: type
built-in.description: A Java class, interface, enum, record or annotation.

built-in.name: CONTAINS
built-in.description: The subject contains the object, for example a module contains a package.

built-in.name: DEPENDS_ON
built-in.description: The subject needs the object to build or run.

built-in.name: CALLS
built-in.description: The subject invokes the object at runtime.

built-in.name: EXTENDS
built-in.description: The subject type extends the object type.

built-in.name: IMPLEMENTS
built-in.description: The subject type implements the object interface.

maven-extractor.name: artifact
maven-extractor.description: A Maven artifact that none of the analyzed repositories builds, such as a third-party library. Its key is groupId:artifactId.

maven-extractor.name: BUILD_DEPENDS_ON
maven-extractor.description: The subject module declares a Maven dependency on the object module or artifact.

scope.description: The Maven scope, such as compile, runtime or test.

version.description: The version the build asks for, if known.

optional.description: Present and true for an optional dependency.

artifactType.description: The artifact type if not jar, such as test-jar or pom.

coordinates.description: The groupId:artifactId the POM declares, when it differs from the object module's own: JitPack coordinates naming an analyzed repository.

maven-extractor.name: PACKAGES
maven-extractor.description: The subject service packages the object library as its main code, so the two form one deployable (a thin service repository and its .lib artifact).

maven-extractor.name: version
maven-extractor.description: The version the subject's build declares.

maven-extractor.name: packaging
maven-extractor.description: The Maven packaging of the subject module, such as jar, war or pom.

maven-extractor.name: java-release
maven-extractor.description: The major Java release the subject module compiles for, such as 21, from the compiler plugin's release, maven.compiler.release, the plugin's source, maven.compiler.source or java.version, in that order.

maven-extractor.name: deployable-by
maven-extractor.description: What makes the subject module deployable: war or ear packaging, spring-boot (an executable jar repackaged by Spring Boot's plugin), quarkus, shade or assembly (a jar with a main class), or an image built by spring-boot-build-image, jib, jkube or docker.

maven-extractor.name: parent
maven-extractor.description: The coordinates of the subject module's parent POM, groupId:artifactId:version, as its POM writes them.

maven-extractor.name: coverage-tool
maven-extractor.description: A coverage tool the subject module's build runs, by its Maven plugin's groupId:artifactId, such as org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin.

goals.description: The goals the plugin's executions bind, sorted. Absent when none is bound in the POM read.

limits.description: For JaCoCo, the limits of the rules its check goal enforces, each with element, counter, value and minimum or maximum as strings, JaCoCo's defaults filled in. Absent when there are none.

java-extractor.name: method
java-extractor.description: A method or constructor of a Java type. Its key is the declaring type's binary name, '#', the method's name (<init> for a constructor) and its erased parameter types in parentheses, such as com.example.Order#total(java.lang.String,int[]).

java-extractor.name: field
java-extractor.description: A field or enum constant of a Java type. Its key is the declaring type's binary name, '#' and the field's name.

java-extractor.name: kind
java-extractor.description: What sort of thing the subject is. For a Java type: class, interface, enum, record or annotation. For a schema: how it is migrated, flyway, liquibase or sql (other SQL files), one fact for each.

java-extractor.name: generated
java-extractor.description: The Java type is generated code, and by what: the generator its @Generated annotation names, such as org.mapstruct.ap.MappingProcessor, or build for a type in the build's generated sources that names none.

config-extractor.name: config-value
config-extractor.description: A config property of the subject module, from its application and bootstrap files (or of the subject config repository, for the application named in the attribute application), as Spring Boot sees it: by default, or with the attribute profile active. The value has its placeholders resolved; one that cannot be resolved, such as an environment variable no file sets, stays as ${KEY}.

key.description: The property key as Spring Boot flattens it, such as spring.application.name or shop.hosts[0].

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one. Absent for the default view; present only where the value differs from it.

written.description: The value as written, when it differs from the resolved value.

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders that could not be resolved.

source.description: Present when the value is not one of the subject module's own config files: environment-post-processor for a default a library adds in code, through an EnvironmentPostProcessor, which has the lowest precedence in a unit that bundles the library; config-repository for a value a Spring Cloud Config repository serves, whose subject is the repository and which outranks the application's own files.

application.description: For a config-repository value: the application its file is named after, or application for the files every application gets.

masked.description: Present and true when the key names a secret written in the file, so the value is not recorded.

docs-extractor.name: readme
docs-extractor.description: A README file in a repository, read as low-trust documented claims. Its key is the repository's name, ':' and the file's path in the repository, such as orders:README.md.

docs-extractor.name: document
docs-extractor.description: A Markdown or AsciiDoc document in a repository that is neither a README nor a decision record: one in a doc, docs, documentation or architecture folder, or named ARCHITECTURE. Read as low-trust documented claims. Its key is the repository's name, ':' and the file's path in the repository, such as orders:docs/architecture/overview.md.

docs-extractor.name: decision
docs-extractor.description: An architecture decision record (ADR) in a repository. Its key is the repository's name, ':' and the file's path in the repository, such as orders:docs/adr/0001-use-kafka.md.

docs-extractor.name: claim
docs-extractor.description: Something the subject document says, one paragraph, list item, table row or quote in its Markdown or AsciiDoc as written. A documented claim, not checked against the code.

section.description: The heading the claim is under, if any.

docs-extractor.name: diagram
docs-extractor.description: A diagram the subject document draws: the source of a code block in a diagram language, or of a plain one drawn as boxes, as written. A documented claim, not checked against the code.

section.description: The heading the diagram is under, if any.

language.description: The diagram's language, such as mermaid or plantuml, or text for one drawn with box characters.

docs-extractor.name: title
docs-extractor.description: The subject's title, as written, without a leading number.

docs-extractor.name: decision-number
docs-extractor.description: The number of the subject decision record, from its file name or else its title, such as 12 for 0012-use-kafka.md.

docs-extractor.name: decision-status
docs-extractor.description: The status the subject decision record states, as written, such as Accepted, proposed or Superseded by ADR-0005.

docs-extractor.name: decision-date
docs-extractor.description: The date the subject decision record states, as written, such as 2024-03-01.

docs-extractor.name: decision-context
docs-extractor.description: The context or problem statement of the subject decision record: the Markdown of its Context (or Context and Problem Statement) section.

docs-extractor.name: decision-outcome
docs-extractor.description: What the subject decision record decided, and why where it says: the Markdown of its Decision (or Decision Outcome) section.

docs-extractor.name: decision-consequences
docs-extractor.description: The consequences the subject decision record states: the Markdown of one of its Consequences sections.

sql-extractor.name: schema
sql-extractor.description: The database schema a build module's migrations build: Flyway migrations, Liquibase changelogs or other SQL files. Its key is the module's groupId:artifactId, or the repository name for a repository without modules. It has no C4 level: which data store holds it is decided from the datasource configuration, since several schemas may share one database.

sql-extractor.name: table
sql-extractor.description: A table of a schema. Its key is the schema's key, ':' and the table name as the database folds it (unquoted names in lower case), qualified with a database schema when the migrations name one, such as com.acme:orders-app:orders. It has no C4 level: a table is part of a data store.

sql-extractor.name: column
sql-extractor.description: A column of a table. Its key is the table's key, '#' and the column name, such as com.acme:orders-app:orders#id.

sql-extractor.name: PRIMARY_KEY
sql-extractor.description: The subject table's primary key includes the object column.

columns.description: All the key's column names, in key order.

name.description: The constraint name, if the migrations give one.

sql-extractor.name: UNIQUE_KEY
sql-extractor.description: A unique key of the subject table includes the object column. A table may have several; the columns attribute tells them apart.

columns.description: All the key's column names, in key order.

name.description: The constraint name, if the migrations give one.

sql-extractor.name: REFERENCES
sql-extractor.description: A foreign key of the subject table references the object table. The object may be a table the schema does not create.

columns.description: The subject table's column names, in key order.

referencedColumns.description: The object table's column names, in the same order; absent when the key names none and the object's primary key is not known.

name.description: The constraint name, if the migrations give one.

sql-extractor.name: data-type
sql-extractor.description: The SQL type of the subject column as the migrations write it, in lower case, such as varchar(200) or bigint.

sql-extractor.name: nullable
sql-extractor.description: Whether the subject column accepts null.

sql-extractor.name: position
sql-extractor.description: The subject's place among its siblings, from 1. For a column, its place in its table.

spring-extractor.name: stereotype
spring-extractor.description: The Spring stereotype of the subject type, a bean class: controller, service, repository, configuration or component, the most specific its annotations carry, directly or through meta-annotations. A Jakarta REST resource (a class with @Path, on it or a supertype) is a controller.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written on the type that makes it one, such as a custom annotation carrying @RestController.

via.description: The meta-annotations leading from that annotation to the stereotype, in order. Absent when the stereotype is written directly.

rest.description: Present and true for a controller whose handler methods write their response to the body (@RestController or @ResponseBody), or a Jakarta REST resource.

spring-extractor.name: main-class
spring-extractor.description: The subject type is an application's main class: spring-boot for a Spring Boot application class (@SpringBootApplication or @EnableAutoConfiguration, directly or through meta-annotations), java for another class with a main(String[]) method.

main.description: The entity ID of the type's main(String[]) method. Absent for a Spring Boot application class without one.

spring-extractor.name: entry-point
spring-extractor.description: The subject method is where work starts in a running application, such as a request handler, a scheduled job or a message listener. Its subtypes say which kind. Values resolved from config are those of the default view unless profile is set.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the value was resolved. Absent for the default view; present only where the value differs from it.

written.description: The value as written in the code, when it differs from the resolved value (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder named a secret, so the value is recorded as written, not resolved.

spring-extractor.name: endpoint
spring-extractor.description: The subject method handles HTTP requests: the HTTP method and path, such as POST /api/orders, or the path alone when it takes any method. The path joins the controller's and the method's mappings, with placeholders resolved against the config of the controller's module.

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method, such as GET. Absent when the mapping takes any method.

controller.description: The binary name of the controller class, which differs from the method's own type when the method is inherited.

annotation.description: The binary name of the mapping annotation on the method, such as org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping.

framework.description: Which annotations map the request: Spring MVC or WebFlux request mappings, or Jakarta (or javax) REST.

spring-extractor.name: scheduled
spring-extractor.description: The subject method runs on a schedule (@Scheduled, JobRunr's @Recurring or a request scheduled recurrently, or a Quartz job whose cron was found): the cron expression, or the delay or rate, with placeholders resolved against the config of the method's module.

timeUnit.description: The unit of a delay or rate when written, such as SECONDS. Milliseconds when absent.

framework.description: The job library, for a job of JobRunr or Quartz. Absent for @Scheduled.

request.description: A JobRunr request handler's request type, the binary name.

job.description: A Quartz job's class, the binary name.

scheduledBy.description: The IDs of the methods whose code sets the job up: passes its request to the scheduler, or builds its Quartz job and trigger. Absent when none is found in the analyzed code.

spring-extractor.name: background-job
spring-extractor.description: The subject method runs as a background job that a library starts, not on a cron, delay or rate: a JobRunr request handler's run method (the job runs when its request is enqueued or scheduled once), an @Job method, a @Recurring interval, or a Quartz job whose cron was not found. The value is the job's name, interval or class.

kind.description: What the value is: the job (its @Job name, its request type or its Quartz class), or a @Recurring interval.

request.description: A JobRunr request handler's request type, the binary name.

job.description: A Quartz job's class, the binary name.

scheduledBy.description: The IDs of the methods whose code sets the job up: passes its request to the scheduler, or builds its Quartz job and trigger. Absent when none is found in the analyzed code.

spring-extractor.name: profile-gate
spring-extractor.description: The subject bean class or @Bean method is only registered when the profile expression matches the active profiles (@Profile, directly or through a meta-annotation), such as audit, !prod or (a) | (b) for several.

profiles.description: The profile expressions as written; any one matching is enough.

annotation.description: The binary name of the custom annotation carrying @Profile, when it is not written directly.

spring-extractor.name: bean
spring-extractor.description: The subject method defines a Spring bean (@Bean); the value is the bean's name, the first name the annotation gives or else the method's name.

spring-extractor.name: aspect
spring-extractor.description: The subject type is an AspectJ aspect (an @Aspect class) with advice (@Before, @After, @AfterReturning, @AfterThrowing, @Around). It runs around the methods its pointcuts select, which ADVISES lists; an aspect that enforces access (a permission or membership check) is a component of the units whose entry points it advises.

advice.description: The kinds of advice the aspect has: before, after, after-returning, after-throwing, around.

pointcuts.description: The pointcut expressions of its advice, as written.

annotations.description: The binary names of the annotations its pointcuts select methods or types by (@annotation, @within, @target), such as a permission annotation. Absent when none.

spring-extractor.name: ADVISES
spring-extractor.description: The subject aspect's advice selects the object method: the aspect runs around its calls. Read from the advice's pointcut (@annotation, @within, @target, within and execution designators, and named pointcuts) against the methods of the analyzed code, including other repositories.

advice.description: The entity ID of the advice method.

spring-extractor.name: property-gate
spring-extractor.description: The subject bean class or @Bean method is only registered when the properties named have the value given (@ConditionalOnProperty, directly or through a meta-annotation). The value is the properties joined by & and, when given, =havingValue.

properties.description: The full property keys, the prefix joined to each name.

havingValue.description: The value the properties must have; absent when any value but false will do.

matchIfMissing.description: Present and true when the bean is registered also when the property is not set.

annotation.description: The binary name of the custom annotation carrying @ConditionalOnProperty, when it is not written directly.

spring-extractor.name: discovery-client
spring-extractor.description: The subject main class registers its unit with service discovery (@EnableDiscoveryClient or the older @EnableEurekaClient). A unit also registers with no annotation, through a discovery client starter alone; joining the two is the linker's. The value is discovery.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation.

autoRegister.description: Present and false when the annotation turns registration off.

spring-extractor.name: infrastructure-server
spring-extractor.description: The subject main class makes its unit an infrastructure server: a Eureka server (@EnableEurekaServer), a config server (@EnableConfigServer) or a Spring Boot Admin server (@EnableAdminServer). The value is eureka, config or admin.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation.

spring-extractor.name: access-check
spring-extractor.description: Callers of the subject method, or of every method of the subject class, must pass the access check its method security annotation states: @PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize, @Secured, @RolesAllowed, @PermitAll or @DenyAll, directly or through a meta-annotation. The value is the expression or roles as written, else the kind. It is enforced only where method security is on (method-security).

annotation.description: The binary name of the custom annotation carrying the check, when it is not written directly.

spring-extractor.name: method-security
spring-extractor.description: The subject class turns method security on for the units that load it (@EnableMethodSecurity, @EnableReactiveMethodSecurity or the older @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity), so access-check annotations of the kinds it enables are enforced. The value is on.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation.

spring-extractor.name: advised-by
spring-extractor.description: An aspect's advice applies to the subject method because of the annotation at this line, which its pointcut selects by @annotation, @within or @target, such as a custom permission check. The value is the aspect's binary name. The ADVISES relation states the same from the aspect's side, at the advice.

advice.description: The entity ID of the advice method.

annotation.description: The binary name of the selecting annotation.

spring-extractor.name: SCHEDULES
spring-extractor.description: The subject method schedules the object job method (JobRunr or Quartz) at the call this fact cites. The job's own fact names its schedulers as scheduledBy.

persistence-extractor.name: datasource
persistence-extractor.description: A datasource URL in the subject module's config, such as jdbc:postgresql://shop-db:5432/shop, without credentials (no user or password before the host, and no user, password or other secret property), by default or with the attribute profile active. Placeholders that cannot be resolved stay as ${KEY}.

key.description: The config key, such as spring.datasource.url.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one. Absent for the default view; present only where the datasource differs from it.

technology.description: The database the URL, or else the driver class configured with it, names, such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.

server.description: The host and port as the URL writes them, such as shop-db:5432.

database.description: The database, service or schema name the URL names, such as shop.

written.description: The URL as written, without credentials, when it differs from the resolved value.

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders that could not be resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a secret was substituted into the URL, so it is recorded as written, placeholders kept; or ****** when a credential might be left in it.

persistence-extractor.name: MAPS_TO
persistence-extractor.description: The subject entity class is stored in the object table: a JPA @Entity, with its table named as Spring Boot's default naming makes it (or as written, when the module's config sets another physical naming strategy), a Spring Data relational @Table class, a MongoDB @Document (its collection) or an Elasticsearch @Document (its index); collection and index names are kept as written. The table is keyed by the module that declares the entity; the linker matches it to the tables migrations create by name.

namingStrategy.description: The physical naming strategy of the code's own that the module's config sets, when it is neither Spring Boot's default nor Hibernate's standard one; the name is then recorded as the entity gives it.

inheritedFrom.description: The binary name of the entity at the top of its single-table inheritance hierarchy, whose table it shares.

persistence-extractor.name: REPOSITORY_FOR
persistence-extractor.description: The subject Spring Data repository interface stores the object entity type, its domain type.

base.description: The binary name of the Spring Data interface it extends, such as org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository, or of @RepositoryDefinition.

persistence-extractor.name: READS_TABLE
persistence-extractor.description: The subject method (or type, for code outside methods) runs SQL that reads the object table: through JdbcTemplate, NamedParameterJdbcTemplate, JdbcClient or R2DBC's DatabaseClient, a repository's native @Query, a MyBatis @Select, @Insert, @Update or @Delete, or a statement of a MyBatis XML mapper (on its mapper interface's method). The table is keyed by the module whose code runs the SQL.

statement.description: The kind of SQL statement: select, insert, update, delete, merge, upsert or truncate.

api.description: The binary name of the type whose method takes the SQL, or of the @Query or MyBatis annotation, or org.apache.ibatis.session.SqlSession for an XML mapper's statement.

persistence-extractor.name: WRITES_TABLE
persistence-extractor.description: The subject method (or type, for code outside methods) runs SQL that writes the object table, the target of an insert, update, delete, merge, upsert or truncate: through JdbcTemplate, NamedParameterJdbcTemplate, JdbcClient, R2DBC's DatabaseClient or SimpleJdbcInsert, a repository's native @Query, a MyBatis @Select, @Insert, @Update or @Delete, or a statement of a MyBatis XML mapper (on its mapper interface's method). The table is keyed by the module whose code runs the SQL.

statement.description: The kind of SQL statement: insert, update, delete, merge, upsert or truncate.

api.description: The binary name of the type whose method takes the SQL or the table name, or of the @Query or MyBatis annotation, or org.apache.ibatis.session.SqlSession for an XML mapper's statement.

persistence-extractor.name: data-store
persistence-extractor.description: A non-relational store the subject module's config connects it to (MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Cassandra, Neo4j or Couchbase), by default or with the attribute profile active: its URI without credentials, or one made of the host, port and database keys (such as mongodb://localhost:27017/shop). Placeholders that cannot be resolved stay as ${KEY}.

key.description: The config key it is read from: the URI's, else the host's or the database's, such as spring.data.mongodb.uri.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one. Absent for the default view; present only where the store differs from it.

server.description: The host and port, the first when the store names several (a MongoDB replica set, a list of Elasticsearch URIs, Cassandra contact points), such as mongo:27017.

database.description: The database, keyspace or bucket, such as shop.

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders that could not be resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a secret was substituted into it, so it is recorded as written, without credentials.

http-client-extractor.name: http-call
http-client-extractor.description: The subject method (or type, for code outside methods) sends an HTTP request: the HTTP method and URL, such as POST http://payments:8080/api/payments, or the URL alone when the method is not known. Placeholders are resolved against the config of the code's module; one nothing resolves is kept as written (${TAX_SERVICE_URL}), and an expression the extractor does not follow is shown as its source in braces ({productId}). User information, query and fragment are left out of every URL. A Feign client called by name goes to http://<name>, as Spring Cloud OpenFeign sends it. Values are those of the default view unless profile is set.

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method, such as GET. Absent when the code does not say which.

path.description: The URL's path, starting with /: everything after the scheme and authority, or after a leading placeholder or expression that stands for them. Absent when a placeholder or expression stands for the whole URL.

url.description: The whole URL, when it starts with a scheme.

baseUrl.description: The URL's scheme and authority, such as http://payments:8080, when it starts with a scheme.

service.description: The client name the request is sent to, matched against a service's spring.application.name: a Feign client's name, or the host of a load-balanced client's URL or of an lb:// URL.

loadBalanced.description: Present and true when the request goes through a load-balanced client (a @LoadBalanced RestTemplate, RestClient or WebClient bean or builder, or an lb:// URL): its host is a service name resolved through discovery, recorded as service when it is written out (not a placeholder).

client.description: What sends the request: a Spring Cloud OpenFeign or MicroProfile REST client interface, a Spring HTTP interface (@HttpExchange), RestTemplate, RestClient, WebClient, the Jakarta (or javax) REST client API, java.net.http, OkHttp or Apache HttpClient.

clientType.description: The binary name of the client interface, for a declarative client; it may differ from the method's own type when the method is inherited.

annotation.description: The binary name of the mapping annotation on a client interface's method, such as org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping.

expressions.description: The source of the parts of the URL the extractor did not follow, as they appear in braces in it.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the URL was resolved. Absent for the default view; present only where the URL or service differs from it.

written.description: The URL as written in the code, when it differs from the resolved one (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder named a secret, so the URL is recorded as written, not resolved, without path, url, baseUrl or service.

http-client-extractor.name: http-client
http-client-extractor.description: The subject interface is a declarative HTTP client: feign for a Spring Cloud OpenFeign client (@FeignClient), microprofile-rest-client for a MicroProfile REST client (@RegisterRestClient), http-interface for a Spring HTTP interface (@HttpExchange on the interface or its methods). Its methods carry the http-call facts. The code that enables or injects it, not the library that declares it, makes its calls (ENABLES, INJECTS).

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written on the interface that makes it a client, which may carry @FeignClient as a meta-annotation; for an HTTP interface without one on the interface, the annotation on its first mapped method, such as org.springframework.web.service.annotation.GetExchange.

http-client-extractor.name: ENABLES
http-client-extractor.description: The subject type turns on the object client interface, as @EnableFeignClients does for the clients it lists or that are in its packages, or as code that makes an HTTP interface's proxy does (HttpServiceProxyFactory.createClient), so the application the subject belongs to makes the client's calls.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written on the subject, which may carry @EnableFeignClients as a meta-annotation. Absent when member is set.

member.description: The entity ID of the method, constructor or type whose code makes an HTTP interface's proxy. Absent when annotation is set.

http-client-extractor.name: INJECTS
http-client-extractor.description: The subject type has the object client interface injected, through a field or a constructor parameter of that type, so its code calls the client.

member.description: The entity ID of the field or constructor that takes the client.

http-client-extractor.name: http-client-bean
http-client-extractor.description: The subject @Bean method makes an HTTP client or a builder of one, which code elsewhere injects to send requests: rest-template (RestTemplate, RestOperations, RestTemplateBuilder), rest-client (RestClient or its builder) or web-client (WebClient or its builder). The object is the client kind.

type.description: The binary name of the type the method returns.

loadBalanced.description: Present and true when the method is @LoadBalanced: the hosts of the URLs its clients send to are service names, resolved through discovery (Spring Cloud LoadBalancer).

baseUrl.description: The base URL the method's code sets (baseUrl, rootUri, create), as written, placeholders kept. Absent when none is set.

messaging-extractor.name: message-listener
messaging-extractor.description: The subject method handles messages from a broker (@KafkaListener, @JmsListener, @RabbitListener, directly, through a meta-annotation, or on its class with @KafkaHandler or @RabbitHandler; or a Spring Cloud Stream input binding of a function bean or a @StreamListener): the topic, topic pattern, queue or destination it listens on, one fact for each, with placeholders resolved against the config of the method's module.

broker.description: Which messaging API the listener uses.

destinationKind.description: What the value names: a Kafka topic or topic pattern, a RabbitMQ queue, or a JMS destination (a queue or a topic, as the listener container decides).

group.description: The Kafka consumer group: groupId, or else the listener's id; for a Spring Cloud Stream binding, its group. Absent when none is written.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written that makes the method a listener. Absent for a Spring Cloud Stream function, which none does.

binding.description: The Spring Cloud Stream binding the method consumes, such as process-in-0, whose config gives the destination (its own name when none is configured) and group. Absent outside Spring Cloud Stream.

anonymous.description: Present and true for a Spring Cloud Stream RabbitMQ binding without a group: the binder declares an anonymous queue, named here as the destination with .anonymous, whose real name ends in a random suffix.

followed.description: The entity IDs of the fields or parameters whose @Value gave a value, when a value was followed from one.

messaging-extractor.name: message-send
messaging-extractor.description: The subject method sends messages to a broker, through a Kafka, JMS or RabbitMQ template or producer, or as a listener's reply (@SendTo), or through a Spring Cloud Stream output binding (a function bean's, StreamBridge.send or a legacy @Output channel): the topic, destination, exchange or queue it sends to, with constants folded, placeholders resolved and a value followed one hop from a @Value field or parameter. A send through the RabbitMQ default exchange is recorded as a send to the queue its routing key names. Values resolved from config are those of the default view unless profile is set.

broker.description: Which messaging API the send uses.

destinationKind.description: What the value names: a Kafka topic, a RabbitMQ exchange, a RabbitMQ queue (through the default exchange), or a JMS destination.

routingKey.description: The routing key of a send to a RabbitMQ exchange. Absent when it is not known.

routingKeyWritten.description: The routing key as written in the code, when it differs from the resolved one.

template.description: The binary name of the type whose method sends, such as org.springframework.kafka.core.KafkaTemplate or org.springframework.cloud.stream.function.StreamBridge, the legacy binding interface whose @Output channel is used, or the @SendTo annotation for a reply. Absent for a Spring Cloud Stream function's output.

method.description: The name of the method called, such as convertAndSend. Absent for @SendTo.

binding.description: The Spring Cloud Stream binding sent through, such as supply-out-0, or the name given to StreamBridge.send; its config gives the destination, else the name is the destination. Absent outside Spring Cloud Stream.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the value was resolved. Absent for the default view; present only where the value differs from it.

written.description: The value as written in the code or the @Value it was followed from, or for a Spring Cloud Stream binding in the config property that sets its destination, when it differs from the resolved value (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder named a secret, so the values are recorded as written, not resolved.

followed.description: The entity IDs of the fields or parameters whose @Value or assignment gave a value, when a value was followed from one.

unknown.description: The values the send has that could not be told, such as routingKey, when the code passes one that cannot be followed.

messaging-extractor.name: message-binding
messaging-extractor.description: The subject method binds a RabbitMQ queue to an exchange (BindingBuilder, new Binding, or @QueueBinding on a listener; or, for a Spring Cloud Stream input binding, the queue the binder declares for the binding's group, bound to the destination's exchange): the queue's name, with the exchange and the routing key or pattern, constants folded, placeholders resolved and a value followed one hop from a @Value field or parameter. Values resolved from config are those of the default view unless profile is set.

broker.description: Which broker the binding is for.

exchange.description: The exchange the queue is bound to.

exchangeWritten.description: The exchange as written, when it differs from the resolved one.

exchangeType.description: The exchange's type, such as topic, direct, fanout or headers, when known. A topic exchange matches routing keys against the binding's pattern with * and # wildcards.

routingKey.description: The binding's routing key or pattern, such as order.*. Absent for a fanout or headers exchange, or when not known.

routingKeyWritten.description: The routing key as written, when it differs from the resolved one.

binding.description: The Spring Cloud Stream binding the queue is declared for. Absent outside Spring Cloud Stream.

anonymous.description: Present and true when the queue is a Spring Cloud Stream binding's anonymous one, named as the destination with .anonymous; its real name ends in a random suffix.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the value was resolved. Absent for the default view; present only where the value differs from it.

written.description: The queue's name as written, when it differs from the resolved one (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder named a secret, so the values are recorded as written, not resolved.

followed.description: The entity IDs of the fields or parameters whose @Value or assignment gave a value, when a value was followed from one.

messaging-extractor.name: message-destination
messaging-extractor.description: The subject method (or type, for a field initializer) declares a destination of a broker, whether or not anything binds, sends to or listens on it: a RabbitMQ queue or exchange (new Queue, QueueBuilder, new TopicExchange and the other exchange classes, ExchangeBuilder, also inside a Declarables or another call's arguments) or a Kafka topic (TopicBuilder.name, new NewTopic). The object is its name, constants folded, placeholders resolved and a value followed one hop from a @Value field or parameter. Values resolved from config are those of the default view unless profile is set.

broker.description: Which broker the destination is declared on.

exchangeType.description: For an exchange, its type, such as topic, direct, fanout or headers, when known.

durable.description: For RabbitMQ, whether the queue or exchange survives a broker restart, when the declaration tells.

deadLetterExchange.description: For a queue, the exchange its rejected and expired messages go to (deadLetterExchange, or the x-dead-letter-exchange argument, given to withArgument or in a Map.of of withArguments or the Queue constructor); empty for the default exchange.

deadLetterRoutingKey.description: For a queue, the routing key its dead letters are sent with (deadLetterRoutingKey, or the x-dead-letter-routing-key argument).

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the value was resolved. Absent for the default view; present only where the value differs from it.

written.description: The name as written, when it differs from the resolved one (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder named a secret, so the values are recorded as written, not resolved.

followed.description: The entity IDs of the fields or parameters whose @Value or assignment gave a value, when a value was followed from one.

mail-extractor.name: mail-send
mail-extractor.description: The subject method sends mail: through a mail library (Spring's JavaMailSender or MailSender, Jakarta Mail's Transport, Apache Commons Email, Simple Java Mail, Quarkus's or Micronaut's mailer), whose server comes from the config (spring.mail.host) or a mail-host fact, or through a mail provider's SDK (SendGrid, Amazon SES, Mailgun), which names the provider (ADR 0076).

template.description: The binary name of the type whose method sends, such as org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSender.

method.description: The name of the method called, such as send.

provider.description: The mail provider an SDK sends through, such as SendGrid, Amazon SES or Mailgun; absent for a mail library.

mail-extractor.name: mail-host
mail-extractor.description: The subject method sets the mail server's host as a constant, such as smtp.example.com: through JavaMailSenderImpl.setHost, Apache Commons Email's setHostName or Simple Java Mail's MailerBuilder.withSMTPServer (ADR 0076).

template.description: The binary name of the type whose method sets the host, such as org.springframework.mail.javamail.JavaMailSenderImpl.

method.description: The name of the method called, such as setHost.

identity-extractor.name: jwt-secret-key
identity-extractor.description: The subject method makes an HMAC key for signing or checking JWTs from a secret in config: jjwt's Keys.hmacShaKeyFor, signWith, setSigningKey or verifyWith, Nimbus's MACSigner or MACVerifier, Spring Security's withSecretKey or java-jwt's Algorithm.HMAC256. The value is the first config key the secret comes from; the secret's value is never recorded (ADR 0085).

library.description: The JWT library: jjwt, nimbus-jose-jwt, spring-security or java-jwt.

call.description: The call that takes the secret, such as Keys.hmacShaKeyFor.

keys.description: The config keys of the @Value placeholders the secret comes from, such as app.token.signing.key.

uses.description: What the code of the method's type does with JWTs: sign, verify or both. Absent when it does neither where the extractor sees it.

identity-extractor.name: identity-admin-client
identity-extractor.description: The subject method builds an identity provider's admin client, Keycloak's (KeycloakBuilder.serverUrl, Keycloak.getInstance). The value is the server's URL as written: a @Value text with its placeholders, which the linker resolves through the unit's config, or a literal URL without credentials (ADR 0085).

product.description: The identity provider, such as Keycloak.

identity-extractor.name: jwt-decoder
identity-extractor.description: The subject method builds Spring Security's JWT decoder, which checks tokens with an identity provider's keys: NimbusJwtDecoder or NimbusReactiveJwtDecoder withJwkSetUri, withIssuerLocation or withPublicKey, or JwtDecoders and ReactiveJwtDecoders fromIssuerLocation. The value says where the keys come from: jwk-set-uri, issuer or public-key (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

call.description: The call that builds the decoder, such as NimbusJwtDecoder.withJwkSetUri.

url.description: The JWK set's or issuer's URL as written, a @Value text with its placeholders or a literal URL without credentials; absent when the code passes it on from elsewhere.

keys.description: The config keys of the @Value placeholders the URL comes from.

identity-extractor.name: http-security
identity-extractor.description: The subject sets up how callers sign in or show a token: a method using Spring Security's HttpSecurity or ServerHttpSecurity DSL, or a type annotated with legacy Spring Security OAuth's @EnableAuthorizationServer, @EnableResourceServer, @EnableOAuth2Sso or @EnableOAuth2Client. The value is one of oauth2-login (users sign in through an OAuth2 or OIDC provider), oauth2-resource-server (callers show a provider's token), oauth2-client, oauth2-authorization-server (the subject's unit issues tokens), form-login, http-basic, saml2-login, x509, one-time-token-login or webauthn (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

via.description: HttpSecurity (servlet), ServerHttpSecurity (reactive) or annotation (legacy Spring Security OAuth).

call.description: The DSL call or annotation, such as oauth2Login or @EnableResourceServer.

identity-extractor.name: jwt-key-pair
identity-extractor.description: The subject method signs or checks JWTs with the key of a key pair: Nimbus's RSASSASigner, RSASSAVerifier, ECDSASigner or ECDSAVerifier. The value is the kind of key, RSA or EC; a key's value is never recorded (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

call.description: The constructor, such as new RSASSASigner.

keys.description: The config keys of the @Value placeholders the key comes from, when the extractor can follow it.

identity-extractor.name: identity-client
identity-extractor.description: A client that a Keycloak realm export in the subject repository registers: an application that signs users in or gets tokens there. The value is its client ID; its secret is never recorded (ADR 0085, amended for #395).

realm.description: The realm the export is of.

public.description: Whether the client is public (no secret, such as a browser or mobile app).

flows.description: The flows it may use: authorization-code, implicit, password, client-credentials.

pkce.description: The PKCE challenge method it requires, such as S256.

redirectUris.description: Where the provider may send users back to, without credentials.

bearerOnly.description: Present and true when the client only checks tokens and never signs users in (Keycloak's legacy bearer-only clients).

rootUrl.description: The application's root URL as the export gives it, without credentials; it may hold ${ENV} placeholders.

baseUrl.description: The application's base URL as the export gives it, without credentials.

webOrigins.description: The browser origins the provider allows for the client.

redis-extractor.name: repo
redis-extractor.description: A repository of the snapshot, the subject of facts about files that belong to no module, such as a compose file in a deployment repository. Its key is the repository's name, as in the summaries. It has no C4 level.

redis-extractor.name: redis-use
redis-extractor.description: The subject (a method, a type or a module) uses Redis in the way the value names: template (operations on Redis through a Spring Data Redis template), hash (a @RedisHash type kept as Redis hashes), session (Spring Session's Redis store), rate-limiter (the gateway's RedisRateLimiter), lock (a Redis lock registry), cache (a Redis cache manager, spring.cache.type=redis, @EnableCaching, or a Spring or JCache cache annotation or Cache call in a module whose cache provider is Redis), pubsub (publishing or subscribing to channels) or client (a Redis client among the module's dependencies). Which server is the config's; the linker matches them.

api.description: The binary name of the type whose method or annotation it is, or the dependency's artifact ID.

operation.description: What the call does with the data.

structure.description: The Redis data structure the operation is made on: value, hash, list, set, zset, stream, geo or hyperloglog.

key.description: The key as the code writes it, with * for what it does not write out, such as bff:session:*.

channel.description: The channel a message is published to, written as for key.

hash.description: The keyspace of a @RedisHash type: its value, else its class name.

namespace.description: The Redis namespace a Spring Session store is configured with.

ttl.description: The time to live written out, such as 600s or 30m.

source.description: Present when the use is shown by a dependency or by config rather than by code.

configKey.description: The config key that shows the use.

cache.description: The Spring cache a cache annotation or call names (constants folded), kept in Redis under <cache>::<key>.

people-extractor.name: person-evidence
people-extractor.description: The subject (a type, a method or a repository) shows that people use the system in the way the value names: role (a role or authority that Spring Security, Jakarta or a Keycloak realm names), membership (a type about members of something, such as an organization), invitation (a type about invitations people receive), route (a screen of a frontend, by its path), account (an endpoint where people sign up, sign in, confirm an account or reset a password, or a Keycloak realm that lets people register) or role-type (a constant of the enum that types the roles of a user account the system keeps). It records only what the code says; the linker decides which people it makes of it.

name.description: For a role, the role as the code names it, without the ROLE_ prefix. For role-type: the enum constant.

source.description: For a role, where it is named: the annotation (PreAuthorize, PostAuthorize, Secured, RolesAllowed), the security call (hasRole, hasAnyRole, hasAuthority, hasAnyAuthority) or keycloak-realm. Also DeclareRoles, isUserInRole and isCallerInRole for role, and keycloak-realm for account.

serviceAccountOnly.description: For a Keycloak realm role, present and true when only service accounts hold it, so it names software, not a kind of person.

scope.description: For a membership, the word before Member in the type's name, such as Organization; absent when the name has none.

type.description: For a membership or an invitation, the binary name of the type. For role-type: the enum.

path.description: For a route, the path as the frontend's router writes it. For account: the endpoint's full path.

framework.description: For a route, the router: angular, react or vue.

action.description: For account: what a person does there: signs up, signs in, confirms an account or resets a password.

summary.description: For account: the endpoint's OpenAPI summary, in the code's own words.

guard.description: For account: the roles that guard the endpoint; one guarded only by a role for software is not a person's.

field.description: For role-type: the account's field that holds the role.

annotation.description: For role: the custom annotation that carries the check, when it is not written directly.

anyReceiver.description: For role: true when the check is a hasRole-like call on a type of the system's own or the servlet's (isUserInRole), not Spring Security's.

deployment-extractor.name: deployment-container
deployment-extractor.description: A container that a deployment descriptor of the subject repository runs in one environment: a compose service, or a container of a Kubernetes workload from a kustomize overlay, a Helm chart or a plain manifest. The value is its name: the compose container name or service, or the workload's name (with the container's after a slash when the pod has several). The linker ties it to the deployable unit it runs and to the data stores the units' config leaves open.

platform.description: What runs it: Docker Compose, Kubernetes manifests (kustomize or plain) or a Helm chart.

environment.description: The environment within its platform: the compose file's suffix (docker-compose.local.yml is local, a plain compose file default), the kustomize overlay's folder, the chart's name with a values file's suffix, or default for plain manifests.

kind.description: service for compose, else the Kubernetes workload kind, such as Deployment or StatefulSet.

image.description: The image as written, with variables resolved from a committed .env file or their defaults and Helm values filled in; an unset variable stays ${NAME}.

product.description: The product the image is, when Lantern knows it, such as PostgreSQL or RabbitMQ.

version.description: The version the image's tag starts with, such as 17.5 for postgres:17.5-alpine3.22.

role.description: What the product is to the system: database, cache, broker, identity, proxy, discovery, observability, mail, storage or runtime.

build.description: A compose service's build context, with its Dockerfile after a space when one is named.

hosts.description: The names other containers of the environment reach it by: the compose service, container name, hostname and network aliases; the workload's name, its StatefulSet service and the Services that select its pods.

aliases.description: Other names it goes by that are not hosts: its pod's app labels and its container's name.

env.description: Its environment variables as the descriptor sets them: a compose env_file and the ConfigMaps a Kubernetes container takes them from included; values with credentials in a URL have them left out.

masked.description: Environment variables and properties it sets whose values are not recorded: secret ones by name or value, and those taken from a Kubernetes Secret or the pod's fields.

ports.description: Its ports as written: a compose service's published ports (host:container), a Kubernetes container's container ports.

dependsOn.description: The compose services it starts after.

composeProfiles.description: The compose profiles it runs under; without any it always runs.

databases.description: The databases it creates on start: the one an official image's variable names (POSTGRES_DB, MYSQL_DATABASE, MARIADB_DATABASE, MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE) and those its init scripts create.

replicas.description: The replicas a Kubernetes workload asks for.

properties.description: Spring properties the last stage's ENTRYPOINT and CMD set when they run java (-Dkey=value, --key=value), and -D options in its JAVA_OPTS, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS; secret ones are masked.

activeProfiles.description: The Spring profiles it makes active: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE, or the spring.profiles.active property, when written out (not a placeholder).

deployment-extractor.name: dockerfile
deployment-extractor.description: A Dockerfile of the subject repository; the value is its path. Evidence is its last FROM line, the stage that becomes the image.

from.description: The base image of the last stage, ARG defaults filled in.

technology.description: The product and version of the base image when Lantern knows it, such as Eclipse Temurin 21.

exposes.description: The ports the last stage exposes.

env.description: The variables the last stage's ENV instructions set; secret ones are masked.

masked.description: Variables and properties it sets whose values are not recorded because they are secrets.

properties.description: Spring properties the last stage's ENTRYPOINT and CMD set when they run java (-Dkey=value, --key=value), and -D options in its JAVA_OPTS, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS; secret ones are masked.

activeProfiles.description: The Spring profiles it makes active: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE, or the spring.profiles.active property, when written out (not a placeholder).

deployment-extractor.name: deployment-route
deployment-extractor.description: A route into the system that a Kubernetes Ingress or Gateway API HTTPRoute of the subject repository declares; the value is its host (or *) and path, such as api.example.com/orders.

environment.description: The environment, as for a deployment container.

class.description: An Ingress's ingressClassName, such as nginx.

gateway.description: The Gateway an HTTPRoute attaches to (its first parentRef).

host.description: The host it matches, if any.

pathType.description: How the path matches: Prefix, Exact or ImplementationSpecific for an Ingress; PathPrefix, Exact or RegularExpression for an HTTPRoute.

port.description: The Service's port, by number or name.

rewrite.description: The path it rewrites to: the nginx rewrite-target annotation, or an HTTPRoute URLRewrite filter's replacePrefixMatch or replaceFullPath.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend
frontend-extractor.description: A frontend: a single-page app that runs in the browser, built from a package manifest (package.json) that depends on Angular, React or Vue. Its key is the repository's name, with the folder of the manifest after a slash when it is not at the top of the repository, such as shop/web-ui. A container of the diagrams, one per frontend.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-app
frontend-extractor.description: The subject is a frontend built with the framework the value names (angular, react or vue), read from its package manifest, with how it is built and served.

name.description: The name documents show: the manifest's name without an npm scope, else the folder's or repository's name.

directory.description: The folder of the manifest in the repository; empty at its top.

framework.description: The framework's name: Angular, React or Vue.

version.description: The framework's major and minor version from the range the manifest asks for, such as 19.2 for ^19.2.0.

libraries.description: Libraries Lantern knows among its dependencies (UI kits, build tools, HTTP and WebSocket clients), by name, such as PrimeNG or STOMP.js.

image.description: The base image of the last stage of the Dockerfile in its folder, the one that serves it.

server.description: The product that image is, such as nginx.

technology.description: Its technology as a diagram shows it: the framework and version, the build tool, and the server, such as Angular 19.2 · nginx.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-call
frontend-extractor.description: The subject frontend's code calls a URL from the browser: an HTTP request (Angular's HttpClient, fetch, axios) or a WebSocket it opens (WebSocket, SockJS, a STOMP client's brokerURL). The value is the method and URL, or WebSocket and the URL, as the default build resolves it.

httpMethod.description: The HTTP method; absent for a WebSocket.

url.description: The URL with constants and the default build's environment values filled in: absolute, or a path the page's own origin serves. What stays unknown is written {name}; a query is left out.

alternates.description: The other URLs the call has with the values of the other environment files, when they differ.

navigation.description: True when the code navigates the browser to the URL (window.location.href, location.assign or replace), leaving the app for a page the server answers, rather than requesting it from the page.

written.description: The URL's expression as the code writes it.

unresolved.description: Environment values the URL needs that no environment file sets.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-proxy
frontend-extractor.description: Requests from the subject frontend's page to a path prefix (the value, such as /api/) are passed on to another server: by the nginx that serves it (proxy_pass), or by its development server (an Angular proxy config, Vite's server.proxy, a package manifest's proxy).

target.description: The URL requests are passed to, as written.

source.description: What passes them on: the nginx that serves the frontend, or the development server.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-url
frontend-extractor.description: The subject frontend's calls build their URLs from a value its code or an environment file declares at this line: a constant or field of the call's file, or an entry of an Angular environment file or a dotenv file. The value is the value as declared.

name.description: The constant's, field's or entry's name.

source.description: constant for a constant or field of the call's file; environment for an environment entry.

defaultBuild.description: Present and true for an environment entry of the build the frontend uses by default.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-auth
frontend-extractor.description: How the subject frontend signs its requests or guards its pages: an Angular HTTP interceptor (functional or a class) or a route guard, from its declaration to the end of its body. The value is interceptor or guard. A guard decides only what the browser shows; it is not access control.

type.description: For a guard, the kind: CanActivate, CanActivateChild, CanMatch or CanDeactivate.

headers.description: For an interceptor, the headers it sets on requests.

bearer.description: Present and true when an interceptor sends a Bearer token.

withCredentials.description: Present and true when an interceptor sends the browser's cookies.

storage.description: Where an interceptor reads its token: localStorage or sessionStorage and the key, such as localStorage:token.

redirect.description: For a guard, the path it sends the browser to when it refuses.

routes.description: For a guard, the route paths that use it.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-component
frontend-extractor.description: An Angular page or part of one (an @Component class, value component) or a service (an @Injectable class, value service) of the subject frontend, from its decorator to the end of its class.

injects.description: The types it injects, through inject() or its constructor.

calls.description: The methods it calls on what it injects, as Type.method.

routes.description: For a component, the route paths that show it.

frontend-extractor.name: frontend-resource
frontend-extractor.description: An absolute URL the subject frontend's templates or styles make the browser load: the src or href of a tag that loads what it names (an image, script, stylesheet, frame or media; not a link a user follows), or a CSS url(). The value is the URL without its query.

tag.description: The tag that loads it, such as img or link, or css for a style's url().

perItem.description: Present and true when the URL is joined to an expression, so each item the page shows loads its own, as with an image service.

gateway-extractor.name: gateway-route
gateway-extractor.description: A Spring Cloud Gateway route: requests matching its predicates go, through its filters, to its URI. The value is the route's id. The subject is the method that builds it with RouteLocatorBuilder, or the module whose config (spring.cloud.gateway.routes, or the server.webflux, server.webmvc or mvc forms, or Netflix Zuul's zuul.routes) defines it. Placeholders in the URI are resolved against the config of the module; values are those of the default view unless profile is set.

definedIn.description: Where the route is defined: in code, with RouteLocatorBuilder, or in config.

framework.description: zuul for a route of Netflix Zuul's config (zuul.routes): its URI is its url, else lb:// and its serviceId or name; its path is behind zuul.prefix; the parts Zuul strips are a StripPrefix filter. Absent for Spring Cloud Gateway.

uri.description: The URI requests go to, such as lb://main-service, lb:ws://notification-service or http://localhost:8081; a placeholder nothing resolves is kept as written, an expression not followed is shown as its source in braces. Absent when masked.

written.description: The URI as written, when it differs from the resolved one (it had placeholders).

unresolved.description: The keys of the placeholders in the URI no config value resolved.

masked.description: Present and true when a placeholder in the URI named a secret, so the URI is recorded as written, without uri.

paths.description: The path patterns of its Path predicates, such as /api/users/**.

methods.description: The HTTP methods of its Method predicates; absent when it takes any.

predicates.description: Every predicate, in order, in the shortcut form config uses, such as Path=/api/files/** or Method=GET,PATCH; or for or-ed predicates in code, or between them.

filters.description: Every route filter, in order: a built-in one in shortcut form, such as StripPrefix=1, or a filter object of the code by its type's simple name, such as AuthFilter.

filterTypes.description: The binary names of the filter classes of the code that the route applies, for a route defined in code.

order.description: The route's order, when one is set.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when the route was read. Absent for the default view; present only where the route differs from it.

gateway-extractor.name: gateway-filter
gateway-extractor.description: The subject class filters requests on their way through a Spring Cloud Gateway or WebFlux application, so work starts in it: global (a GlobalFilter, applied to every route), gateway (a GatewayFilter, applied by the routes that name it), factory (a GatewayFilterFactory, named in route config) or web (a WebFilter, applied to every request). Only classes that are beans, or that a route applies, count.

implements.description: The binary name of the library type the class implements or extends, directly or through classes of the code, such as org.springframework.cloud.gateway.filter.GlobalFilter.

gateway-extractor.name: gateway-discovery-locator
gateway-extractor.description: The subject module's config turns on Spring Cloud Gateway's discovery locator (spring.cloud.gateway.discovery.locator.enabled, or under server.webflux): the gateway routes /<service ID>/** to each service its discovery client knows, without that first segment, unless predicates or filters replace those defaults. The value is the URL expression, by default 'lb://'+serviceId. Values are those of the default view unless profile is set.

lowerCaseServiceId.description: Whether service IDs are put in lower case in paths (Eureka registers them in upper case); absent when not set, which means false.

includeExpression.description: The SpEL expression that picks the services routed to; absent when not set, which means all.

routeIdPrefix.description: The prefix of the ids of the routes it makes, when set.

predicates.description: Predicates that replace the default Path one, in shortcut form, their arguments SpEL over serviceId.

filters.description: Filters that replace the default RewritePath one, in shortcut form, their arguments SpEL over serviceId.

enabled.description: Present and false on a profile's fact when that profile turns off the locator the default view turns on.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one when it was read. Absent for the default view; present only where it differs from it.

test-extractor.name: test-class
test-extractor.description: A top-level class in a module's test sources that declares tests. Its key is the module's groupId:artifactId, ':' and the class's binary name.

test-extractor.name: TESTS
test-extractor.description: The subject test class is in the test sources of the object module, so it tests that module's code.

tests.description: How many tests the class and its member classes declare: test methods, and ArchUnit rule fields.

architecture.description: Present and true when the class's file uses an architecture test library, such as ArchUnit.

test-extractor.name: test-container
test-extractor.description: A container the subject module's tests start: a Testcontainers container or an embedded Kafka broker. The value is its image as written, else its class (EmbeddedKafka for an embedded broker). It shows infrastructure the tests run against, not what production runs. Evidence is its declaration.

class.description: The container's class as written, such as PostgreSQLContainer.

image.description: The image as written in a literal or constant.

technology.description: The product and version when Lantern knows it, such as PostgreSQL 16.

role.description: What the product is to the system: database, cache, broker, identity or cloud.

serviceConnection.description: Present and true when Spring Boot's @ServiceConnection connects the application to it.

embedded.description: Present and true for a broker that runs inside the test, not in a container.

topics.description: The topics an embedded Kafka broker creates, as written.

test-extractor.name: architecture-rule
test-extractor.description: An architecture rule the subject module's tests declare with one of ArchUnit's library rules. The value is its kind: layered, onion or slices. It states what the team intends; Lantern does not run it, so whether the code keeps it is not known. Evidence is the rule's lines.

layers.description: Each layer, onion ring (domainModels, domainServices, applicationServices) or adapter ('adapter <name>'), in the rule's order, as its name and package patterns: {"name": ..., "packages": [...]}.

access.description: Each layer's access rule: ArchUnit's method, such as mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers, then the layers it names.

slices.description: The package pattern whose captures make the slices.

checks.description: What the rule checks of the slices: beFreeOfCycles, notDependOnEachOther.

frozen.description: Present and true when FreezingArchRule.freeze wraps it, so known violations are let be.

ignored.description: Present and true when @ArchIgnore or @Disabled switches it off.

unresolved.description: Present and true when an argument is not a string literal or constant of the file, so it is left out.

websocket-extractor.name: websocket-endpoint
websocket-extractor.description: The subject method registers a WebSocket endpoint that clients connect to: a STOMP endpoint (registry.addEndpoint, @EnableWebSocketMessageBroker) or a raw WebSocket handler (registry.addHandler, @EnableWebSocket). The object is the path. A path registered twice, once plain and once with SockJS, is one fact.

path.description: The path clients connect to, such as /ws-notifications.

protocol.description: stomp for a STOMP endpoint (clients subscribe to destinations and send to application destinations over it), websocket for a raw handler.

sockjs.description: Whether the path is also offered with SockJS fallbacks (withSockJS).

nativeWebSocket.description: Whether the path accepts plain WebSocket connections (a registration without SockJS).

allowedOrigins.description: The origins or origin patterns the registration allows, such as *. Absent when none is set.

handler.description: For a raw WebSocket endpoint, the binary name of the handler's type, when it could be told.

handshakeInterceptors.description: The binary names of the handshake interceptors added to the registration (addInterceptors, or setInterceptors on its SockJS service): code that may refuse the HTTP upgrade or copy request attributes into the session.

handshakeHandler.description: The binary name of the handshake handler set on the registration (setHandshakeHandler), which often decides the connecting user.

websocket-extractor.name: stomp-prefix
websocket-extractor.description: The subject method configures a STOMP destination prefix of the message broker (configureMessageBroker): the prefixes the simple broker or a broker relay serves, the prefix of destinations handled by @MessageMapping methods, or the prefix of user destinations. The object is the prefix.

kind.description: simple-broker: destinations the in-memory broker serves to subscribers; broker-relay: destinations relayed to an external broker; application: destinations that reach @MessageMapping methods; user: the prefix of user destinations.

relayHost.description: For a broker relay, the host of the external STOMP broker (setRelayHost): a constant, or the placeholder of the @Value field it is read from, such as ${relay.host}.

relayPort.description: For a broker relay, the broker's STOMP port (setRelayPort), as a constant or placeholder.

virtualHost.description: For a broker relay, the virtual host on the broker (setVirtualHost).

userDestinationBroadcast.description: For a broker relay, the destination on which unresolved user messages are broadcast to the other instances of the application (setUserDestinationBroadcast); present when several instances share the broker.

userRegistryBroadcast.description: For a broker relay, the destination on which the instances share their user registries (setUserRegistryBroadcast).

websocket-extractor.name: stomp-mapping
websocket-extractor.description: The subject method handles STOMP messages (@MessageMapping) or subscriptions (@SubscribeMapping) sent by a client: the object is the destination, the class's mapping joined with the method's, without the application prefix, which the stomp-prefix facts give.

annotation.description: The binary name of the annotation written.

sendTo.description: The destinations of @SendTo on the method (or its class), where the return value is sent: Spring picks one of the method's or class's @SendToUser and @SendTo, preferring one that names destinations, so this and sendToUser are not both present. Without destinations, or for a @MessageMapping method that returns a value and has neither annotation where a STOMP broker is configured, /topic joined with the destination it handles, Spring's default.

sendToUser.description: The destinations of @SendToUser on the method (or its class), where the return value is sent to the sending user; without destinations, /queue joined with the destination it handles.

defaultSendTo.description: Whether the destination in sendTo or sendToUser is Spring's default rather than written.

repliesToSubscriber.description: For a @SubscribeMapping method that returns a value and has neither @SendTo nor @SendToUser: the value goes back to the subscribing client only, not through the broker.

websocket-extractor.name: stomp-send
websocket-extractor.description: The subject method pushes a message to STOMP subscribers through SimpMessagingTemplate or SimpMessageSendingOperations (convertAndSend, send, convertAndSendToUser): the object is the destination, with constants folded and a part that is not a constant (an id formatted into it) written as {}.

method.description: The name of the method called, such as convertAndSendToUser.

template.description: The binary name of the type whose method sends.

toUser.description: Present and true when the message goes to one user's destination (convertAndSendToUser): subscribers of the user prefix plus the destination.

dynamic.description: Present and true when part of the destination is not a constant, written as {}.

followed.description: The entity IDs of the fields the destination was followed through.

websocket-extractor.name: stomp-interceptor
websocket-extractor.description: The subject method registers a ChannelInterceptor on the STOMP client channel (configureClientInboundChannel or configureClientOutboundChannel), where connect, subscribe and send checks are made. The object is the interceptor's type.

channel.description: The client channel: inbound for messages from clients (CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, SEND), outbound for messages to them.

intercepts.description: The ChannelInterceptor methods the interceptor's class declares, such as preSend. Absent when its class is not in the analyzed sources.

websocket-extractor.name: stomp-channel-interceptor
websocket-extractor.description: The subject class intercepts the messages of a STOMP client channel (it implements ChannelInterceptor, directly or through the application's own types), at its declaration; the object is its binary name. stomp-interceptor facts say on which channel it is registered. Inbound interceptors commonly authenticate CONNECT frames and check which destinations a client may subscribe or send to.

intercepts.description: The ChannelInterceptor methods the class declares, such as preSend.

readsDestination.description: Whether its code reads a message's destination through a STOMP header accessor (getDestination), as a check of what a client may subscribe or send to does.

setsUser.description: Whether its code sets the message's user (setUser), as authentication on CONNECT does.

headers.description: The native STOMP headers its code reads, such as Authorization.

destinations.description: The constant destinations or destination patterns its code names (a text starting with / or ^/), such as the topics it lets clients subscribe to.

deployable-units.name: deployable-unit
deployable-units.description: The subject service is a deployable unit, a container: one runnable application together with the in-set libraries it bundles. The value says what makes it runnable: spring-boot for a Spring Boot application class in its code, war or ear for that packaging, executable-jar for a jar Spring Boot's Maven plugin repackages without such a class.

mainClass.description: The entity ID of the Spring Boot application class that starts it, if one is found.

packaging.description: The Maven packaging of the unit's own module, such as jar or war.

deployable-units.name: application-name
deployable-units.description: The name the subject deployable unit runs under: its spring.application.name, else its Maven artifact ID. Without profile it is the name in the default view; with profile, the name under that profile where it differs.

module.description: The entity ID of the module whose config sets the name: the unit's own module, or a library it bundles when its own module has no config.

profile.description: The profile active instead of the default one. Absent for the default view.

unresolved.description: The keys of placeholders in the name that no config value resolved.

defaulted.description: Present and true when no config sets spring.application.name, so the name is the Maven artifact ID.

deployable-units.name: technology
deployable-units.description: What the subject container is built with or runs on: for a deployable unit such as Spring Boot 3.5.14 / Java 21, for a database the database, such as PostgreSQL.

framework.description: The application framework, such as Spring Boot.

frameworkVersion.description: The framework's version, from the build's dependencies, if known.

frameworks.description: Other frameworks the unit is built on, each with its version when the build states one, such as Spring Cloud Gateway or Eureka Server.

java.description: The major Java release the unit compiles for, if known.

deployable-units.name: BUNDLES
deployable-units.description: The subject deployable unit ships the object in-set library in what it deploys, so the library's code runs as part of the unit. A library can be bundled by several units. This is not a dependency between containers: the two are drawn as one container.

main.description: Present and true when the library holds the unit's main code: the library a thin service packages (PACKAGES), or the one with its application class.

via.description: The entity IDs of the libraries between the unit and this one, in order, when the unit bundles it through them. Absent for a library the unit's own module depends on.

deployable-units.name: version-skew
deployable-units.description: The units that bundle the subject in-set library ask for versions of it other than the one its repository builds at the snapshot's commit, so the code that runs in them is not the code analyzed. The value is the version the library's module declares at that commit.

pins.description: The version each unit that bundles the library asks for, by the unit's entity ID. Units whose dependency names no version are left out.

versions.description: The distinct versions the units ask for, sorted.

cross-repo-links.name: topic
cross-repo-links.description: A Kafka topic, a container of the system. Its key is the broker kind, ':' and the topic name, such as kafka:payments.completed.

cross-repo-links.name: queue
cross-repo-links.description: A message queue, a container of the system. Its key is the broker kind (rabbitmq or jms), ':' and the queue or JMS destination name, such as rabbitmq:payments.order-events.
